text:
Kai: Quick sync — proposal: rotate the golden sample set we use for onboarding benches. Current static goldset is stale and our deepbench cost grows linearly. Idea: rotate ~10% of the goldset weekly, stratified by domain/seqlen, and enforce a tokens/day budget. Feedback?

Maria: +1 on rotation. Need to balance freshness vs detectability of regressions. Why 10%/week as the starting point?

Kai: 10% is a conservative start — keeps long-term comparability while injecting new coverage. We can tune after 4–6 weeks. Also plan to stratify so critical buckets rotate slower (e.g., infra prompts, security-sensitive).

Sanjay: Telemetry-wise we should trigger expedited rotations based on drift signals, not just schedule. Propose metrics: KL divergence on logits, embedding centroid drift, and token entropy change. If KL > 0.05 over a 7d sliding window for a cohort -> expedited rotation.

Ellie: Operational concern: label drift and false positives. For any sample flagged as "high-change" we need a human-review path. Suggest tagging those samples with `needs-review` and routing to the ops queue.

tj: Budget enforcement: implement a scheduler cap, e.g. `max_tokens_per_day: 5000` for deepbench to keep costs predictable. When budget exhausted, fall back to lightweight smoke (shorter inputs, fewer shots).

bench-bot: bench-bot: daily summary 1774660001: deepbench tokens used yesterday 4230 / 5000; cohort alpha KL=0.052 -> expedited rotation recommended.

Maria: What about model variants (quantized vs fp16)? We should keep goldsets per model-variant to avoid misattributing regressions.

Kai: Agreed. Golden indices will carry variant tags, e.g., `mymodel@v12.fp16`, `mymodel@v12.int8`. Fallback policy: if deepbench flags regression on variant but smokebench passes, schedule extended golden for 24h and hold rollout pending human sign-off.

Sanjay: For stochastic models do sampling runs (n=5) and compare distributional metrics rather than exact match. Use aggregated metrics (median BLEU-ish + output entropy delta).

Ellie: Proposed action items: 1) rotation scheduler prototype, 2) telemetry probes for KL/entropy, 3) `needs-review` flag + ops queue wiring, 4) update onboarding playbook and examples. Who picks which?

tj: I can do the scheduler + budget enforcement this week. Will open a small PR with a cron job + token cap and a fallback hook.

Kai: I’ll draft an RFC addendum with explicit thresholds and sample configs. Example config sketch:```
rotation:
  pct_weekly: 0.10
  max_tokens_per_day: 5000
signals:
  kl_threshold: 0.05
  window_days: 7
```

Maria: :thumbsup: If Sanjay and Ellie can own telemetry + review flow we can iterate quickly.

Sanjay: I’ll start a telemetry PR and add the KL/entropy probes to the bench runner.

Ellie: I’ll wire the ops queue and the `needs-review` tag in triage UI.

Kai: Thanks all — will tag you in the RFC draft. If anyone sees edge cases (e.g., multi-lingual coverage, rare-token-heavy prompts) reply here and I’ll fold them into the stratification rules.

tj: quick note — when scheduler is up I’ll include a dry-run mode: `--budget=5000 --dry-run` so we can see what would have rotated before enforcing.

bench-bot: bench-bot: created ticket #B-1423 for expedited rotation flow.
